Quartz Lake Winter Ice Fishing in Alaska

Trade open water for a winter day on Quartz Lake. Ice fishing here puts the focus on a small hole and the next bite below.

About this water

The fishery source record for Quartz Lake, United States, identifies Arctic char, Chinook salmon, Rainbow trout and Coho salmon.

Quartz Lake's agency record describes stocked fish, including char, trout and salmon. Ask which of those fish is the objective of the proposed visit and whether the plan uses open water or a guided winter program. Those options need different equipment and access checks. A stocking record does not establish current fish size, a recent stocking event, or safe ice. Confirm local support before choosing equipment to purchase.

LICENCE & PERMITS

Fishing licence for Alaska

Non-residents aged 16 or older need a sport fishing licence. A king salmon stamp is normally required even when you release the fish.

SHOPPING LIST

Ice fishing shopping list

  • Ice fishing rod and reel combo

    A short 24–32 in rod for jigging through a hole.

    Check price ↗

  • Ice jigs and spoons

    Small tungsten jigs for perch and panfish; spoons for walleye and trout.

    Check price ↗

  • Hand auger or auger blade

    Skip this if your guide drills the holes.

    Check price ↗

  • Ice picks

    Wear them around your neck every time you walk on ice.

    Check price ↗

  • Ice cleats

    Slip-on spikes for bare, slick ice.

    Check price ↗

  • Insulated waterproof boots

    Rated for -40 °F; you stand still for hours.

    Check price ↗

  • Bucket seat with tackle storage

    A seat, a tackle box and a fish bucket in one.

    Check price ↗

  • Skimmer scoop

    Keeps the hole clear of slush.

    Check price ↗

  • Hand and toe warmers

    Cheap and easy to keep in every pocket.
